AUTO-HR • Командная документация
1
AUTO-HR: руководство по проекту для
команды
Архитектура, выполненная работа, результаты экспериментов и план продолжения • 8 октября 2026
Цель проекта
AUTO-HR — система интеллектуального сопоставления резюме с вакансиями. Работодатель
публикует вакансии, кандидат загружает PDF, система рекомендует подходящие позиции и
объясняет результаты через LLM-чат. Сейчас работает CLI-прототип; сайт, ATS-интеграция и
backend API запланированы.
Архитектура
CV PDF → извлечение текста → rule/dictionary skill extraction → multilingual embedding →
гибридное ранжирование относительно 1017 вакансий → Top-10 → выбор вакансии → LLM
Assistant V2. Параллельно: PDF → Rules V2 + LLM V1 → Hybrid V1 → Label Studio → ручная
проверка → BIO/IOB2 → XLM-R NER (план) → интеграция в matcher (план).
Matching
Модель эмбеддингов sentence-transformers/paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2,
размерность 384. Сохранённые эмбеддинги вакансий: (1017,384). Matcher сочетает
семантическую близость и skill overlap. Пример: Data-engineer/Python developer — 53.57%
hybrid score, совпали MySQL, Python, SQL. При отсутствии detected missing skills skill score
может быть ниже 100% из-за confidence adjustment.
LLM-ассистент
После выбора вакансии LLM объясняет конкретный score, релевантные разделы CV,
совпавшие и недостающие требования, опыт. Оценку вычисляет matcher, а не языковая
модель. Доступ к OpenAI API нужен для чата и LLM-аннотатора. Сбой connection reset by peer
на университетском Wi-Fi был сетевым и исчез при смене сети.
Разметка NER
Пять классов: HARD_SKILL (технологии, методы), SOFT_SKILL (личные компетенции),
EXPERIENCE (должности), EDUCATION (программы/квалификации), LANG (заявленные языки).
Rules V2 даёт первые два класса, LLM V1 — последние три. Предсказания импортируются в
Label Studio и обязательно проверяются человеком.
Эксперименты
Pilot CV #1–#5: 220 сущностей. Rules V2: Precision 0.6693, Recall 0.7636, F1 0.7134. LLM V1:
0.5092 / 0.8818 / 0.6456. Hybrid V1: 0.6692 / 0.8000 / 0.7288. Unseen CV #6–#10: 300 human
entities, TP 203, FP 19, FN 97, Precision 0.9144, Recall 0.6767, F1 0.7778. Это небольшой набор;
результаты нельзя считать production benchmark.

AUTO-HR • Командная документация
2
Проблемы качества
CV #13 содержит продублированный извлечённый текст. CV #15 и #18 — буквы разделены
пробелами, что мешает NER. Некоторые EXPERIENCE и EDUCATION размечены ошибочно,
например желаемая должность вместо реальной или профессия внутри другого раздела.
После исправления извлечённого текста offsets необходимо пересчитать.
Что готово
CV parsing, vacancy embeddings, hybrid ranking, Top-10 CLI, выбранная вакансия и LLM chat;
Rules V2, LLM V1, Hybrid V1, Label Studio export/import и строгая оценка. Batch #11–#20
создан, но машинный corrected draft не является human ground truth.
Что дальше — ближайшие задачи
1) Проверить качество PDF text extraction и span offsets. 2) Доработать CV #13, #15, #18 на
этапе preprocessing. 3) Проверить вручную CV #11–#20 и экспортировать human-reviewed
JSON. 4) Провести независимую двойную разметку нескольких CV. 5) Конвертировать span
annotations в BIO/IOB2, разделить train/val/test по документам.
Что дальше — ML и продукт
6) Обучить пилот XLM-R NER и оценить entity-level F1 по пяти классам. 7) Разметить
релевантность пар CV–вакансия и измерить Precision@k, Recall@k, MRR, nDCG. 8)
Спроектировать PostgreSQL/pgvector и API /vacancies, /resumes, /match, /chat. 9) Добавить ATS
sync или admin upload, страницу кандидата, кнопки Ask AUTO-HR и защиту данных.
Как продолжить командой
Открыть репозиторий, проверить git status и структуру ML1/NLP. Команды: python -m
ML1.match_cv "data/resumes/raw/<file>.pdf"; python -m NLP.annotation.evaluate_preannotations
--method hybrid; python -m NLP.annotation.evaluate_unseen_hybrid; conda activate autohr-label;
label-studio start; открыть http://localhost:8080. Команды зависят от фактического состава
клона.
Конфиденциальность
Не публиковать PDF резюме, CSV с личными данными, Label Studio exports и .env в публичном
GitHub. Держать приватный архив и получать согласие на обработку CV. Не применять
match score как автоматическое решение о найме.
Примечание об источниках
Документ составлен по истории разработки и результатам терминальных запусков, без
доступа к полному актуальному репозиторию. Конкретные реализации и сигнатуры функций
необходимо проверить в GitHub. Для продолжения работы ИИ-агентом используйте
отдельный Markdown handover.

High Performance Computing
MPI Exercise
Installing MPI
ForthisexerciseweuseanimplementationoftheMessagePassingInterface(MPI).Therecommended
implementation is Open MPI. After installation, the following commands should be available:
mpic++ mpirun mpiexec
The command mpic++ is used to compile C++ programs that use MPI, whilempirun or mpiexec is
used to start several MPI processes.
Linux / Ubuntu
1 sudo apt update
2 sudo apt install build-essential openmpi-bin libopenmpi-dev
3 mpic++ --version
4 mpirun --version
5 mpic++ -O2 program.cpp -o program
6 mpirun -np 4 ./program
Windows - Recommended Method
For Windows, use WSL with Ubuntu and then install Open MPI inside the Ubuntu terminal.
1 wsl --install
2 sudo apt update
3 sudo apt install build-essential openmpi-bin libopenmpi-dev
4 mpic++ -O2 program.cpp -o program
5 mpirun -np 4 ./program
macOS
Install Homebrew if needed, then install Open MPI:
1 brew install open-mpi
2 mpic++ --version
3 mpirun --version
4 mpic++ -O2 program.cpp -o program
5 mpirun -np 4 ./program
1
Testing the Installation
Create test_mpi.cpp:

12

14 << rank

21 }
Compile and run:
1 mpic++ -O2 test_mpi.cpp -o test_mpi
2 mpirun -np 4 ./test_mpi
A typical output contains four lines such asHello from process 0 of 4 . The order of the four
lines is not guaranteed.
Tasks
The purpose of this exercise is to become familiar with distributed-memory parallel program-
ming using MPI. The work includes ranks, point-to-point communication, broadcast, reduction,
scatter/gather, work decomposition, and timing.
Part 1: MPI Processes and Ranks
Run the test program using 1, 2, and 4 MPI processes.
Number of Processes Rank Values
1 0
2 0, 1
4 0, 1, 2, 3
1. What does MPI_Comm_size() return?
Answer: It returns the total number of processes in the specified communicator.
2
2. What does MPI_Comm_rank() return?
Answer: It returns the unique rank of the calling process inside the communicator.
3. If eight MPI processes are started, what are their possible rank values?
Answer: The ranks are 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, and 7.
4. What is MPI_COMM_WORLD?
Answer: It is the default communicator that contains all MPI processes started together in the
program.
5. Does every MPI process execute the same program?
Answer: Yes. All processes normally start the same executable, but they can perform different
work by checking their rank.
6. Does the order in which the processes print their messages always remain the same?
Answer: No. The order is not guaranteed because the processes execute independently and may
be scheduled differently each time.
3
Part 2: Different Work for Different Processes
Every process calculates
x = (rank + 1)2.
Completed program: hello_mpi.cpp
1 #include <iostream>
2 #include <mpi.h>
3
4 int main(int argc, char* argv[]) {
5 MPI_Init(&argc, &argv);
6
7 int rank;
8 int size;
9 MPI_Comm_rank(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &rank);
10 MPI_Comm_size(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &size);
11
12 int x = (rank + 1) * (rank + 1);
13
14 std::cout << "Process " << rank
15 << ": x = " << x << std::endl;
16
17 MPI_Finalize();
18 return 0;
19 }
For four processes, the expected calculations are:
P0 : 1 2 = 1, P 1 : 2 2 = 4, P 2 : 3 2 = 9, P 3 : 4 2 = 16.
1. Does each process have a different value of rank?
Answer: Yes. Each process has a unique rank inside the communicator.
2. Does every process have its own copy of variablex?
Answer: Yes. Each MPI process has its own address space and therefore its own local copy ofx.
3. Does process 0 directly access the variablex belonging to process 1?
Answer: No. MPI processes have separate memory spaces, so process 0 cannot directly access
process 1’s local variable.
4. Is any communication required for these calculations?
Answer: No. Each process can compute the value independently because the calculation uses only
its own rank.
Part 3: Point-to-Point Communication
Run this part using exactly two processes.
Completed program: send_receive.cpp
1 #include <iostream>
2 #include <mpi.h>
4
3
4 int main(int argc, char* argv[]) {
5 MPI_Init(&argc, &argv);
6
7 int rank;
8 MPI_Comm_rank(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &rank);
9
10 if (rank == 0) {
11 int value = 100;
12 MPI_Send(&value, 1, MPI_INT, 1, 0, MPI_COMM_WORLD);
13 }
14 else if (rank == 1) {
15 int value;
16 MPI_Recv(&value, 1, MPI_INT, 0, 0,
17 MPI_COMM_WORLD, MPI_STATUS_IGNORE);
18 value = value * 2;
19 std::cout << "Result = " << value << std::endl;
20 }
21
22 MPI_Finalize();
23 return 0;
24 }
Expected output from process 1:Result = 200 .
1. Which process is the sender?
Answer: Process 0 is the sender.
2. Which process is the receiver?
Answer: Process 1 is the receiver.
3. Why does the receiver need to know the source process?
Answer: The source rank tells MPI which sender’s message should match the receive operation,
which is especially important when several processes may send messages.
4. What is the purpose of the message tag?
Answer: The tag is an identifier used to distinguish different messages that may be sent between
the same processes.
5. Is this an example of point-to-point or collective communication?
Answer: It is point-to-point communication because one specific process sends data to one specific
receiving process.
5
Part 4: Broadcast
Process 0 initially setsN = 10,000,000, and the value is broadcast to all processes.
Completed program: broadcast.cpp
1 #include <iostream>
2 #include <mpi.h>
3
4 int main(int argc, char* argv[]) {
5 MPI_Init(&argc, &argv);
6
7 int rank;
8 MPI_Comm_rank(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &rank);
9
10 long long N = 0;
11 if (rank == 0) {
12 N = 10000000;
13 }
14
15 MPI_Bcast(&N, 1, MPI_LONG_LONG, 0, MPI_COMM_WORLD);
16
17 std::cout << "Process " << rank
18 << ": N = " << N << std::endl;
19
20 MPI_Finalize();
21 return 0;
22 }
Typical output with four processes contains:
1 Process 0: N = 10000000
2 Process 1: N = 10000000
3 Process 2: N = 10000000
4 Process 3: N = 10000000
1. Which process initially knows the value ofN?
Answer: Only process 0 initially knows the value because it is the process that assignsN =
10,000,000.
2. Which processes knowN after the broadcast?
Answer: All processes inMPI_COMM_WORLD know the value after the broadcast. Each process stores
its own local copy.
3. Does MPI_Bcast() need to be called only by the root, or by all processes?
Answer: It must be called by all processes in the communicator. The root provides the data, and
the other processes participate in receiving it.
4. Why is repeatedly callingMPI_Send() from the root less convenient than using a
broadcast?
Answer: Repeated sends require the root to manage a separate send for every destination.
MPI_Bcast() expresses the one-to-all operation directly and is usually simpler and easier to maintain.
6
Part 5: Parallel Sum

Part 6: Reduction
The local sums are combined usingMPI_Reduce() with MPI_SUM. Only process 0 prints the final
result.
Completed program: parallel_sum.cpp
1 #include <iostream>
2 #include <mpi.h>
3
4 int main(int argc, char* argv[]) {
5 MPI_Init(&argc, &argv);
6
7 int rank, size;
8 MPI_Comm_rank(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &rank);
9 MPI_Comm_size(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &size);
10
11 long long N = 0;
12 if (rank == 0) {
13 N = 10000000;
14 }
15 MPI_Bcast(&N, 1, MPI_LONG_LONG, 0, MPI_COMM_WORLD);
16
17 long long start = rank * N / size + 1;
18 long long end = (rank + 1) * N / size;
19
20 double t0 = MPI_Wtime();
21
22 long long local_sum = 0;
23 for (long long i = start; i <= end; ++i) {
24 local_sum += i;
25 }
26
27 std::cout << "Process " << rank
28 << ": start = " << start
29 << ", end = " << end
30 << ", local sum = " << local_sum
31 << std::endl;
32
33 long long global_sum = 0;
34 MPI_Reduce(&local_sum, &global_sum, 1,
35 MPI_LONG_LONG, MPI_SUM, 0, MPI_COMM_WORLD);
36
37 double t1 = MPI_Wtime();
38 double elapsed = t1 - t0;
39
40 double max_elapsed = 0.0;
41 MPI_Reduce(&elapsed, &max_elapsed, 1,
42 MPI_DOUBLE, MPI_MAX, 0, MPI_COMM_WORLD);
43
44 if (rank == 0) {
45 long long expected = N * (N + 1) / 2;
46 std::cout << "Final result = " << global_sum << std::endl;
47 std::cout << "Expected result = " << expected << std::endl;
48 std::cout << "Execution time = " << max_elapsed << std::endl;
49 }
50
51 MPI_Finalize();
52 return 0;

53 }
The exact verification value is
S = N (N + 1)2 = 50,000,005,000,000.
1. Why can each process calculate its local sum independently?
Answer: Each process receives a separate non-overlapping range of integers, so it can sum that
range without needing data from other processes.
2. What information needs to be communicated after the local calculations are finished?
Answer: The local sums must be communicated and combined so that the program can obtain the
single global sum.
3. What operation doesMPI_Reduce() perform in this program?

Answer: Each process receives a separate non-overlapping range of integers, so it can sum that

2. What information needs to be communicated after the local calculations are finished?

Answer: It applies MPI_SUM to all local sums and produces their total on the root process.

5. What would be different ifMPI_Allreduce() were used instead?
Answer: The same reduction would be performed, but the final global sum would be returned to

1. Does increasing the number of MPI processes always reduce execution time?
Answer: No. More processes can reduce computation time, but communication, synchronization,
process management, and a small problem size can make additional processes provide little benefit
or even increase the total time.
2. Is the speedup equal to the number of processes?
Answer: Usually not. Ideal linear speedup is difficult to achieve because some work is not parallel
and MPI communication introduces overhead.
3. What additional overhead exists in an MPI program that does not exist in the serial
version?
Answer: MPI adds overhead from message passing, synchronization, collective operations, data
movement, process coordination, and MPI runtime management.
4. Why can communication reduce the benefit of parallel computation?
Answer: Communication consumes time without directly performing the target computation.
Processes may also have to wait for data or synchronization, so the communication cost can offset
part of the parallel speedup.

1. What is the purpose ofMPI_Init()?
Answer: It initializes the MPI execution environment and must be called before normal MPI
communication functions are used.
2. What is the purpose ofMPI_Finalize()?
Answer: It terminates the MPI execution environment and performs the final MPI cleanup before
the program exits.
3. What is an MPI rank?
Answer: An MPI rank is the unique integer identifier of a process within a communicator.
4. What is an MPI communicator?
Answer: A communicator is a group of MPI processes together with the communication context in
which they exchange messages and perform collective operations.
5. What is the difference between point-to-point and collective communication?
Answer: Point-to-point communication transfers data between specific sender and receiver processes.
Collective communication involves all processes, or a defined group of processes, in the communicator.
6. What is the difference betweenMPI_Send() and MPI_Bcast()?
Answer: MPI_Send() sends a message from one process to one destination process.MPI_Bcast()
distributes the same data from one root process to every process in the communicator.
7. What is the difference betweenMPI_Reduce() and MPI_Gather()?
Answer: MPI_Reduce() combines process values using an operation such as sum and produces
a reduced result. MPI_Gather() collects the separate values without combining them into one
arithmetic result.
8. Why does MPI work well for distributed-memory systems?
Answer: MPI is designed for processes with separate memory spaces. Processes exchange informa-
tion explicitly through messages, so shared physical memory is not required.
9. What is one important difference between MPI processes and OpenMP threads?
Answer: MPI processes normally have separate address spaces and communicate through messages,
while OpenMP threads normally share the memory of one process.
